Let’s reason step-by-step.

1. 1 AM April 1, 1264 in Europe/Athens → This is before time zones existed, but the question treats it as if modern time zones apply retroactively.
2. Modern time zones:  
   Europe/Athens = EET (UTC+2) or EEST (UTC+3) in summer.  
   US/Eastern = EST (UTC-5) or EDT (UTC-4) in summer.
3. April 1 is likely in EEST (UTC+3) for Athens (summer time starts last Sunday in March in modern times; assume yes for this hypothetical).
4. US/Eastern on April 1 is in EDT (UTC-4) (starts 2nd Sunday in March).
5. Time difference: UTC+3 to UTC-4 = 7 hours behind Athens.
6. 01:00 Athens time − 7 hours = 18:00 previous day (March 31).
7. Date: March 31, 1264, 18:00 (6:00 PM) in US/Eastern.

FINAL_ANSWER: 1264-03-31 18:00
